items.prompt: What does "Kaixo" mean?
items.explanation: "Kaixo" is the most common greeting in Basque, equivalent to "hello".

items.prompt: It's nighttime and you meet a friend. How do you greet them?
items.explanation: "Gabon" is used at night, and also for "good night" when saying goodbye.

items.prompt: "Aspaldiko" means…
items.explanation: "Aspaldiko" is used when you meet someone again after a long time.

items.prompt: Ni Egoitz ___.
items.explanation: "Naiz" is the form of "izan" (to be) for "I".

items.prompt: You want to say "I am Maialen". How do you say it?
items.explanation: For the 1st person singular, we use "naiz".

items.prompt: How do you ask "What's your name?" in Basque?
items.explanation: "Zein" means “which”; "izena" means “the name”; literally “What is your name?".

items.prompt: Nire izena Maialen ___.
items.explanation: "Da" is the 3rd person form of "izan" (to be); the subject here is "izena".

items.prompt: Gu lagunak ___ (we are).
items.explanation: For "we" the form of "izan" is "gara".

items.prompt: What is the form of "to be" for "you (plural)"?
items.explanation: You (plural) = zuek; the verb form is "zarete".

items.prompt: How do you say "I am not a student"?
items.explanation: In Basque, negation follows the pattern: SUBJECT + ez + VERB + attribute.

items.prompt: What does "Nongoa zara?" mean?
items.explanation: "Nongoa" combines "non" (where) + the suffix for origin.

items.prompt: Bilbo + -koa = ___ (from Bilbao).
items.explanation: The suffix "-ko" indicates origin/belonging; with the article "-a" it becomes "-koa".

items.prompt: I live in Donostia = Donostia___ bizi naiz.
items.explanation: For residence, the locative suffix `-(e)n` ("in") is used. Donostia + -n = Donostian (the final "a" is kept).

items.prompt: How do you say "Where do you live?"
items.explanation: "Non" is "where", "bizi zara" is "you live" — literally: "Where do you live?"

items.prompt: Maialen has a sister. What is the word for "sister" from Maialen's point of view?
items.explanation: In Basque, a woman calls her sister "ahizpa"; a man calls her "arreba".

items.prompt: My grandparents = nire ___.
items.explanation: "Aiton-amonak" combines aitona + amona in the plural — a common convention in Basque for pairs.

items.prompt: "Biloba" is...
items.explanation: "Biloba" is grandson/granddaughter. It has no gender marker.

items.prompt: My mother = ___ ama.
How do you say "our house" in Basque?
items.explanation: "Gure" is the possessive for "we".

items.prompt: "Lehengusu" is...
I have two brothers = Bi anaia ___.
items.explanation: "Ditut" = "I have (several)" — form of "ukan" (to have) NOR-NORK.

items.prompt: How do you say "three" in Basque?
What does "Nolakoa zara?" mean?
items.explanation: "Nolakoa" asks about the quality or "what something/someone is like" — a permanent description, not a temporary state.

items.prompt: You want to say "I am tall". How do you say it?
items.explanation: In this pattern, the adjective takes the article `-a`: *altu* + *-a* = *altua*.

items.prompt: Maialen is very nice = Maialen oso atsegin___ da.
items.explanation: Adjective + article `-a` when you describe a quality: *atsegina*.

items.prompt: Hura ___ da. (He is short) — use "baxu" + article.
items.explanation: Standard form: the adjective always with a final `-a`.

items.prompt: How do you say "black hair" in Basque?
items.explanation: *beltz* = black; with the article, *beltza*. The noun "ile" (hair) comes first.

items.prompt: You want to say "I have blue eyes". Which is the correct form?
items.explanation: Eyes are plural ("begi urdinak"), so we use *ditut* (to have several things), not *dut*.

items.prompt: I have long hair = Ile luzea ___.
items.explanation: For "hair" (singular), the form of "ukan" is *dut*.

items.prompt: He/She has green eyes = Begi berdeak ___.
items.explanation: Eyes in plural → 3rd person = *ditu*.

items.prompt: "Alaia" means…
items.explanation: *alaia* is "cheerful". It's one of the most common personality adjectives.

items.prompt: You want to say "My father is hard-working". Which is the correct form?
items.explanation: *langilea* (from *lan*, "work") = hard-working. It goes with *izan*.

items.prompt: Maialen oso ___ da. (Maialen is very nice)
items.explanation: *atsegina* or *jatorra* work for "nice" / "friendly".

items.prompt: Hura isila da, baina ni ___ naiz. (He is quiet, but I am talkative)
items.explanation: *berritsua* = talkative — the opposite of *isila*.

items.prompt: What is the form of "egon" for "I"?
items.explanation: *nago* = "I am". The verb *egon* has its own conjugation, different from *izan*.

items.prompt: You want to say "I am tired". What is the natural form?
items.explanation: For a temporary state ("today I am tired") use *egon* + *nekatuta* (without the final `-a`).

items.prompt: Maialen pozik ___. (Maialen is happy)
items.explanation: *dago* = "is" (3rd person).

items.prompt: Gu nekatuta ___. (We are tired)
items.explanation: *gaude* = "we are".

items.prompt: To say "Maialen is cheerful (in general, it's her nature)" we use…
items.explanation: Stable quality → *izan* + adjective with `-a`.

items.prompt: To say "Today Maialen is happy / content (it's a state)" we use…
items.explanation: Temporary state → *egon* + word without `-a`. *pozik* is the natural choice.

items.prompt: My father is a nervous person (it's his nature) = Nire aita urduria ___.
items.explanation: Quality → *izan*: *da*.

items.prompt: Today my father is nervous (today's state) = Gaur nire aita urduri ___.
items.explanation: Temporary state → *egon*: *dago*. And notice how the adjective loses the `-a`.

items.prompt: We are tired = Nekatuta ___.
items.explanation: Form of *egon* for "we" = *gaude*.

items.prompt: "Kafe hutsa" means…
items.explanation: *hutsa* comes from *huts* ("empty", "pure"): coffee with nothing in it, black coffee.

items.prompt: How do you say "water" in Basque?
items.explanation: *ura* (with the article) or *ur* (without it).

items.prompt: Cider (typical Basque) = ___.
items.explanation: *sagardoa* comes from *sagar* ("apple") + *ardo* ("wine"): apple wine.

items.prompt: Beer = ___.
items.explanation: *garagardoa* comes from *garagar* ("barley") + *ardo*: literally "barley wine".

items.prompt: "Bazkaria" means…
items.explanation: *bazkaria* is the main meal at midday.

items.prompt: How do you say "mid-morning snack" (the 11 a.m. break)?
items.explanation: *hamaiketakoa* (literally: "the one from eleven") is that mid-morning snack, a very Basque custom.

items.prompt: To eat (verb) = ___.
items.explanation: *jan* = to eat. Basic infinitive form.

items.prompt: To drink (verb) = ___.
items.explanation: *edan* = to drink.

items.prompt: "Mesedez" means…
items.explanation: *mesedez* is "please". *Eskerrik asko* is "thank you".

items.prompt: You want to order a coffee. What is the natural formula?
items.explanation: *Kafe bat, mesedez* — "A coffee, please". The noun loses the `-a` when it goes with *bat*.

items.prompt: "I'll have a cortado" = Ebakia ___ ___.
items.explanation: *hartuko dut* = "I'll have". It's a very common way to order.

items.prompt: "Do you want coffee?" = ___ ___ kafea?
items.explanation: *nahi duzu* = "you want". Basic pattern for offering.

items.prompt: "Zenbat balio du?" means…
items.explanation: *zenbat* = how much/how many; *balio* = is worth/costs; *du* = "it has/costs".

items.prompt: How do you say "twenty" in Basque?
items.explanation: *hogei* = 20. It's the base of the Basque vigesimal system.

items.prompt: It costs 3 euros = ___ euro balio du.
items.explanation: *hiru* = 3.

items.prompt: I'll have two coffees = Bi kafe ___ ___.
items.explanation: For "multiple things," you use *ditut* instead of *dut*.

items.prompt: "Ogitarteko" means…
items.explanation: *ogitartekoa* comes from *ogi* (bread) + *arte* (between): "the thing between two breads" — the sandwich.

items.prompt: You want a tortilla pintxo. How do you order it?
items.explanation: "Pintxo bat" loses the `-a` when it goes with *bat*; the descriptor (*tortilla*) goes first.

items.prompt: "Plato combinado" in Basque = ___ ___.
items.explanation: *plater konbinatua* — exactly like in Spanish, without much adaptation.

items.prompt: For me, a portion of cheese = Niretzat ___ ___.
items.explanation: *razioa* = portion; with *bat* it loses the `-a`. The form "gazta razioa" (the portion of cheese) is also valid.

items.prompt: You need to buy bread. What kind of shop do you go to?
items.explanation: "Okindegia" is the bakery. "Oki(n)" is related to "ogi" (bread) — the place of bread.

items.prompt: "Osasun-etxea" is…
items.explanation: "Osasun" means "health" and "etxe(a)" is "house": literally "house of health" = outpatient clinic or health center.

items.prompt: I'm going to withdraw money, I'm going to the bank = ___ noa.
items.explanation: "Banketxe" (bank) + the directional suffix -ra = banketxera, "to the bank".

items.prompt: How do you say "The bar is in the street"?
items.explanation: For "in + place" we add -an to the word: kale + an = kalean ("in the street").

items.prompt: Donostia + locative (in Donostia) = Donostia___.
items.explanation: Words ending in an organic -a only add -n: Donostian.

items.prompt: Madril (Madrid) + locative = Madril___.
items.explanation: After a final consonant, the locative inserts an -e-: Madril → Madrilen.

items.prompt: Question: "Where is the pharmacy?" = ___ dago botika?
"Banketxean nago" means…
items.explanation: "-an" indicates location; "nago" is "I am" (from egon).

items.prompt: "The cat is under the table" — the correct word is:
items.explanation: "Azpian" = under. "Gainean" = on.

items.prompt: How do you say "in front of the church"?
items.explanation: The formula is "X-(r)en + position": elizaren aurrean (of the church + in front).

items.prompt: Mahaiaren ___ daude liburuak (the books are on the table).
"Hemen", "hor", "han" mean, respectively:
items.explanation: The three distances in Basque: HEMEN (near me, "here"), HOR (near the listener, "there"), HAN (far from both, "over there").

items.prompt: How do you ask "Is there a bar in the neighborhood?"
items.explanation: "Bada(go)" expresses existence and "tabernarik" is the partitive "-rik", typical in questions and negations of existence.

items.prompt: "Ez dago supermerkaturik" means…
items.explanation: "Ez dago + X-rik" = "there is no X". The partitive -rik is used with indefinite nouns in negations.

items.prompt: Yes, there is = Bai, ___.
items.explanation: "Badago" is a fusion of "bai dago": the typical affirmative answer to "ba al dago…?".

items.prompt: Negation: There is no bakery here = Hemen ez dago okindegi___.
Key difference between "dago" and "badago":
items.explanation: "Dago" is the neutral form for "it is". "Bada(go)" adds the nuance of existing/"there is"; typically in questions (Ba al dago?) and affirmative answers (Bai, badago).
options: dago = is; badago = is there? or Yes, there is
dago is present, badago is past

items.prompt: You want to say "My neighborhood is small and pretty". How do you say it?
items.explanation: Singular subject with two adjectives: the verb is "da" and the adjectives take a final -a.
options: Nire auzoa txikia eta polita da
Nire auzoa txikiak eta politak dira
Nire auzoan txikia eta polita dago

items.prompt: "In my neighborhood there is a big park" is said:
items.explanation: "Auzo + an" (in the neighborhood) is the location; "parke handi bat" is the subject that exists; "dago" is the verb.
options: Nire auzoa parke handi bat dago
Nire auzoan parke handi bat dago
Nire auzora parke handi bat dago

items.prompt: I live near the center = Erdigunetik gertu ___ naiz.
items.explanation: "Bizi naiz" = "I live". Remember that for "to live in" we always use "bizi".

items.prompt: In my town there is no hospital = Nire herrian ez dago ospitale___.
What question does someone ask to find out where the bakery is?
items.explanation: "Non dago…?" asks for the location of something that is already assumed to exist.

items.prompt: I go = Ni ___.
items.explanation: The synthetic form of "joan" for "I" is "noa". Common in questions like "Nora noa?" → "Where am I going?".

items.prompt: You come = Zu ___.
items.explanation: "Zatoz" is the synthetic form of "etorri" for "zu" (you).

items.prompt: "Nora zoaz?" means…
items.explanation: "Nora" = where to; "zoaz" = you go (synthetic form of "joan" for "zu").

items.prompt: "Sartu" and its opposite "irten" mean, respectively:
How would you say "turn left at the traffic light"?
items.explanation: "Jo ezkerrera" (turn left) + location with "-an": "semaforoan" (at the traffic light).

items.prompt: "Zeharkatu" means…
items.explanation: From "zehar" (across). "Zeharkatu kalea / zebrabidea" = to cross the street / the crosswalk.

items.prompt: Go straight = ___ aurrera.
items.explanation: "Segi aurrera" or "jarraitu aurrera" — both are valid for "go straight."

items.prompt: You want to ask for directions to the hospital. What do you say?
items.explanation: "Non dago…?" asks where something is; ideal for asking for directions.

items.prompt: How do you say "I'm going to Bilbao"?
items.explanation: "Bilbo" + the -ra suffix (NORA case) = "Bilbora", "to Bilbao".

items.prompt: I'm going home = Etxe___ noa.
items.explanation: "Etxe" + ra = "etxera" (to home). The -ra suffix is the NORA case.

items.prompt: I'm going to Madrid = Madril___ noa.
items.explanation: After a consonant, the suffix adds an -e-: "Madril" → "Madrilera".

items.prompt: What does "Eskolara doa" mean?
items.explanation: "Eskola" + ra (NORA case) = "eskolara" (to the school); "doa" = "he/she goes".
options: He/She is going to the school
He/She is coming from the school

items.prompt: We're going to the park = Parke___ goaz.
What does "Zertara zoaz tabernara?" mean?
items.explanation: "Zertara" = what for (to do what); you typically answer with a verb + -tzera: "kafe bat hartzera" (to have a coffee).
options: Who is going to the bar?
Which bar are you coming from?
What are you going to the bar for?

items.prompt: "I come from Bilbao" is said:
items.explanation: "Bilbo" + suffix -tik = "Bilbotik" (from Bilbao, origin of the movement).

items.prompt: I come from home = Etxe___ nator.
items.explanation: "Etxe" + tik = "etxetik" (from home, origin).

items.prompt: They come from Madrid = Madril___ datoz.
items.explanation: After a consonant, the suffix adapts: "Madril" → "Madrildik" or "Madriletik" (both forms are accepted).

items.prompt: What does "Lanetik nator" mean?
items.explanation: "Lan" + etik = "lanetik" (from work, origin). "Nator" = I come (synthetic etorri).

items.prompt: Combine origin and destination: "I come from the bank and I'm going to the supermarket":
items.explanation: NONDIK = -tik (origin, with etorri); NORA = -ra (destination, with joan). Bankutik nator + supermerkatura noa.

items.prompt: Question: Where do you come from? = ___ zatoz?
How do you say "I'm going by bus"?
items.explanation: "Autobus" + suffix -ez (instrumental) = "autobusez" (by bus, mode of movement).

items.prompt: I'm going on foot = ___ noa.
items.explanation: "Oinez" is the set form for "on foot" (literally "with foot").

items.prompt: I'm going to Pamplona by train = Iruñera ___ noa.
"Bilbora hegazkinez doaz" means…
items.explanation: Bilbo + ra = to Bilbao; hegazkin + ez = by plane; doaz = they are going.
options: They are coming from Bilbao by plane
They are going to Bilbao by plane
He/She is on the plane to Bilbao

items.prompt: How do you ask "How do you go to school?"
items.explanation: "Nola?" means "how?". To ask about the means of transport, we use "Nola zoaz…?" or also "Zerez zoaz?".

items.prompt: What does "Zer ordu da?" mean?
items.explanation: "Zer" = what; "ordu" = hour; "da" = is. Literally: "What hour is it?".

items.prompt: It's one o'clock. How do you say it?
items.explanation: One o'clock is special: you say "ordu bata da" (singular, with the article "-a").

items.prompt: It's five o'clock. How do you say it?
items.explanation: From two o'clock onwards, the hours in Basque are plural: "bostak dira" (literally: "they are the fives").

items.prompt: It's eight o'clock = Zortziak ___.
items.explanation: "Dira" is the 3rd person plural of the verb "izan". The hours (except for one o'clock) are plural.

items.prompt: It's half past five. How do you say it in Basque?
items.explanation: For "half past" you use "eta erdiak" (literally "and halves", also plural). The number goes without "-ak" before "eta erdiak": "bost eta erdiak".

items.prompt: It's a quarter past three. How do you say it?
items.explanation: "Eta laurden" means "and a quarter"; the hour is plural ("hirurak"): *Hirurak eta laurden dira*.

items.prompt: It's a quarter to nine. How do you say it?
items.explanation: In Basque, "to" is expressed with "gutxi", and it goes at the end. Literally: "the nines quarter less".

items.prompt: It's five past seven = Zazpiak eta ___ dira.
items.explanation: Minutes past are said with "eta + number". Five = bost.

items.prompt: It's ten to four = Laurak hamar ___ dira.
items.explanation: "Gutxi" means "to" or "less" in time expressions.

items.prompt: "Goizean" means…
items.explanation: "Goiz" = morning; with the locative "-an": "in the morning".

items.prompt: You want to say "eight in the morning". How do you say it?
items.explanation: To specify morning/afternoon, you place the part of the day with the suffix "-ko" before the time: *goizeko zortziak* (eight in the morning).

items.prompt: In the afternoon = ___ (fill in the full word).
items.explanation: "Arratsalde" = afternoon; with the locative "-(e)an": *arratsaldean* (in the afternoon).

items.prompt: At night = ___ (fill in the full word).
items.explanation: "Gau" = night; with the locative "-an": *gauean*.

items.prompt: What does "esnatzen naiz" mean?
items.explanation: The habitual aspect (-tzen + naiz/dut) expresses what you normally do: "I wake up" (every day).
options: I am going to wake up

items.prompt: "Egunero gosaltzen dut" means…
items.explanation: "Egunero" = every day; "gosaltzen dut" = I have breakfast (habitually).
options: I am going to have breakfast

items.prompt: Esnatu (to wake up) → habitual form ___ (with the -n of the habitual aspect).
items.explanation: Verbs ending in a consonant or in -tu/-du add "-tzen" for the habitual aspect: esna**tu** → esna**tzen**.

items.prompt: Jan (to eat) → habitual form ___ (with the habitual aspect ending).
items.explanation: Verbs ending in -n change: ja**n** → ja**ten** (not "janten"). The rule: final -n → "-ten".

items.prompt: "Zer ordutan esnatzen zara?" means…
items.explanation: "Zer ordutan…?" = "what time…?". The suffix "-tan" functions as "at (the hour)".
options: What time do you wake up?
When do you go to bed?
What do you have for breakfast?

items.prompt: How would you say "I wake up at seven"?
items.explanation: To say "at (time)", you use "-etan" on the plural form of the hour: zazpi**etan** = at seven.

items.prompt: At nine o'clock = ___ (fill in the full word).
items.explanation: The time "at X o'clock" is formed with "-(e)tan": *bederatzi* + *-etan* = *bederatzietan*.

items.prompt: In the morning I go to work = Goizean ___ joaten naiz.
items.explanation: "Lan" = work. With the NORA case (-ra, direction): *lanera* = "to work".

items.prompt: "Zer egin duzu gaur?" means…
items.explanation: "Egin" is the participle of "to do"; "duzu" is the ukan form for "you". Together = "you have done".
options: What do you do every day?
What are you going to do tomorrow?

items.prompt: Compare: "egunero gosaltzen dut" vs "gaur gosaldu dut". What's the difference?
items.explanation: This is the key: the participle + auxiliary WITHOUT -tzen is the recent past. With -tzen it's habitual.
options: The first is present, the second is future
The first is habitual (I have breakfast every day), the second is recent past (I have had breakfast today)
The second one is not correct
They both mean the same thing

items.prompt: I have eaten = jan ___ (auxiliary for "I + object").
items.explanation: "Jan" (to eat) is transitive: it takes ukan. "I" → *dut*. Result: *jan dut* (I have eaten).

items.prompt: I have gone = joan ___ (auxiliary for "I" without an object).
items.explanation: "Joan" (to go) is intransitive: it takes izan. "I" → *naiz*. Result: *joan naiz* (I have gone).

items.prompt: "Egunkaria irakurri dut" means…
items.explanation: "Irakurri" (to read) + "dut" (I + object) = "I have read". Without -tzen, it marks the recent past.
options: I read the newspaper every day
I am going to read the newspaper

items.prompt: How would you say "Mikel has had breakfast at home"?
items.explanation: *Gosaldu* is transitive (it takes an implicit object: breakfast). The subject takes the NORK case (-k): *Mikelek*; the auxiliary is *du*.

items.prompt: We have bought bread = Ogia erosi ___.
items.explanation: "Erosi" takes ukan; "we" → *dugu*. Subject: *guk*. Result: *guk ogia erosi dugu*.

items.prompt: They have drunk wine = Ardoa edan ___.
items.explanation: "Edan" takes ukan; "they" → *dute*. Subject: *haiek*. Result: *haiek ardoa edan dute*.

items.prompt: "Etxera joan naiz" means…
items.explanation: "Joan" + "naiz" without -tzen marks the recent past: "I have gone". The destination takes -ra: *etxera* (to the house / home).

items.prompt: Why does "joan" use the auxiliary naiz and not dut?
items.explanation: Verbs without an object (to go, to come, to wake up...) take izan (naiz/zara/da). Those that have an object take ukan (dut/duzu/du).
options: Because it's an intransitive verb (it doesn't take an object)
Because it's a first conjugation verb

items.prompt: You want to say "Maialen has come late". How do you say it?
items.explanation: *Etorri* (to come) is intransitive: it takes *izan*. "She" → *da*. Without -k on the subject. Result: *Maialen berandu etorri da*.

items.prompt: I have woken up late = Berandu esnatu ___.
items.explanation: "Esnatu" (to wake up) is intransitive: it takes izan; "I" → *naiz*.

items.prompt: They have gone to the cinema = Zinera joan ___.
items.explanation: "Joan" takes izan; "they" → *dira*. Result: *haiek zinera joan dira*.

items.prompt: "Atzo arratsaldean" means…
items.explanation: "Atzo" = yesterday; "arratsaldean" = in the afternoon. Combined: "yesterday afternoon".

items.prompt: You want to say "This morning I had breakfast at home". How do you say it?
items.explanation: "Gaur goizean" = "today in the morning / this morning". And since it's the recent past, "gosaldu dut" without -tzen.

items.prompt: Distinguish: "askotan" vs "behin". What do they mean?
items.explanation: "Askotan" = often, many times. "Behin" = once (it usually accompanies one-off actions).
options: They both mean the same thing

items.prompt: The day after tomorrow = ___ (fill in the word).
items.explanation: "Etzi" = the day after tomorrow. The time sequence: atzo (yesterday) → gaur (today) → bihar (tomorrow) → etzi (the day after tomorrow).

items.prompt: What is the correct translation of 'I woke up late this morning'?
items.explanation: *Esnatu* is intransitive (it takes *izan*); 'I' → *naiz*. 'This morning' → *gaur goizean*.

items.prompt: In the sentence *Mikelek egunkaria irakurri du*, why does *Mikelek* have a -k?
items.explanation: In Basque, the subject of transitive verbs takes the NORK marker (-k): *Mikel**ek*** has read the newspaper.
options: Because it's the subject of a transitive verb (NORK)
It's a mistake, it should just be Mikel

items.prompt: I had toast and coffee for breakfast = *Tostadak eta kafea* ___ ___ (fill in: participle + auxiliary for 'I').
items.explanation: For 'to have/eat several things', *ditut* is used (plural auxiliary of *ukan*): *hartu/jan ditut*.

items.prompt: I walked to the euskaltegi = *Euskaltegira oinez* ___ ___ (fill in: participle + auxiliary).
items.explanation: *Joan* (intransitive) + *naiz* for 1st person = *joan naiz*.

items.prompt: You want to take a shower. Which room do you go to?
items.explanation: "Komuna" is the bathroom (the room with a shower, sink, etc.).

items.prompt: "Egongela" is...
items.explanation: "Egongela" is composed of "egon" (to be) + "gela" (room) — the room where you 'are', the living room.

items.prompt: We sleep in the ___ (in English: bedroom).
items.explanation: "Logela" = "lo" (sleep) + "gela" (room).

items.prompt: In which room is the "hozkailua"?
items.explanation: "Hozkailua" (fridge) is always in the kitchen (sukaldean).

items.prompt: "Gau-mahaia" means…
items.explanation: "Gau" = night, "mahaia" = table. Literally "night table".

items.prompt: I have two beds in my house = Bi ohe ___ etxean.
items.explanation: "Ditut" = "I have (several things)" — verb "ukan" with a plural object.

items.prompt: How do you say "to do the dishes"?
items.explanation: "Ontziak garbitu" (literally "to clean the dishes") = to do the dishes. You can also say "harrikoa egin".

items.prompt: "Ohea jantzi" is...
items.explanation: "Jantzi" means to dress/to put on; "ohea jantzi" = to put on/make the bed.

items.prompt: I clean the bathroom = Nik komuna ___.
items.explanation: For a habitual action, we use `-tzen` + auxiliary verb (present tense): "garbitzen dut" = I clean.

items.prompt: The suffix -rekin (sociative) means…
items.explanation: "-rekin" indicates company: "lagunarekin" = "with the friend".

items.prompt: I live with my parents = Gurasoe___ bizi naiz.
items.explanation: In the plural, the suffix is "-ekin": guraso + -ekin = gurasoekin (with the parents).

items.prompt: "Bikotekidearekin bizi naiz" means...
items.explanation: "Bikotekide" = partner (literally: "member of the couple"). With -arekin = "with the partner".

items.prompt: To ask "How many rooms does it have?" you say…
items.explanation: "Zenbat" = how much/many, "gela" = room, "ditu" = it has (multiple objects).

items.prompt: My house is bright = Nire etxea ___ da.
items.explanation: "Argitsua" = bright (from "argi" = light + the suffix -tsu for abundance).

items.prompt: "Etxea hirugarren solairuan dago" means...
items.explanation: "Hirugarren" = third, "solairua" = floor, "dago" = it is. "It's on the third floor".
options: The house is on the third floor

items.prompt: Who is your "bizilaguna"?
items.explanation: "Bizi" (to live) + "laguna" (companion) = "living companion" → neighbor (in your building or neighborhood).

items.prompt: "Lankidea" is made up of…
items.explanation: "Lan" (work) + "kide" (member/companion) = "coworker".

items.prompt: My koadrila = nire ___.
items.explanation: "Koadrila" is a loanword from the Spanish "cuadrilla", and in the Basque Country it is central to social life.

items.prompt: Who is a "polizia"?
items.explanation: "Polizia" = police officer. It's a loanword, but the Basque form with the article is "polizia" (without an additional final -a).

items.prompt: A "Mekanikaria" works with...
items.explanation: "Mekanikaria" is a mechanic; they usually work in garages with cars.

items.prompt: I am a student = Ni ___ naiz.
items.explanation: "Ikaslea" = student. Remember: in Basque, "I am X" is said "Ni X-a naiz", with the noun + article "-a".

items.prompt: How do you introduce someone who is next to you? "This is my friend"
items.explanation: To introduce someone, you use the demonstrative "hau" (this) + subject + "da" (third-person singular).

items.prompt: He is my neighbor = ___ nire bizilaguna da.
items.explanation: "Bera" or "hura" mean he/she in Basque. "Bera" is the most common form in everyday speech.

items.prompt: "Bera nire lankidea da" means...
items.explanation: "Bera" = he/she, "lankidea" = coworker, "da" = is.

items.prompt: How do you say "He/she works at the hospital"?
items.explanation: "Ospitalean" = at the hospital (locative -ean), "lan egiten du" = he/she works (3rd person).

items.prompt: He/she lives in Pamplona = Iruñean ___ da.
items.explanation: "Bizi da" = he/she lives (literally: "is living"). For the 1st person it would be "bizi naiz".

items.prompt: "Bera euskaltegian lan egiten du" — which profession fits best?
items.explanation: If they work at an euskaltegi, they are most likely a teacher (irakaslea).

items.prompt: He/she is 40 years old = Berrogei urte ___.
items.explanation: "Ditu" = he/she has (3rd person, plural object — years are counted in the plural).

items.prompt: To introduce an elderly neighbor who lives alone, what order is most natural?
items.explanation: First you introduce them (Hau X da), then you add details (Bera Y da), and finally you say what they do (Bera Z egiten du).
options: Hau ... da → bera ... da → bera ... egiten du
Bera ... egiten du → hau ... da → bera ... da
Hura ... egiten du → hau ... naiz → bera ... zara
Ni ... naiz → zu ... zara → bera ... da

items.prompt: "Nire bizilaguna 75 urteko jubilatua da" means…
items.explanation: "75 urteko jubilatua" = a 75-year-old retiree. Structure: "X-eko Y" indicates age/attribute + noun.
options: My neighbor is 75 years old and is retired

items.prompt: My neighbors are nice = Nire bizilagunak ___ dira.
items.explanation: "Atseginak" or "jatorrak" are the two most common adjectives for "nice/pleasant" in the plural.

items.prompt: Where do you buy bread?
items.explanation: "Okindegia" comes from *ogi* (bread); the suffix *-degi* means "place where there is…".

items.prompt: You want to buy *legatza* (hake). Which shop do you go to?
items.explanation: *Arrandegia* comes from *arrain* (fish). The suffix *-ra* indicates destination: "I'm going to the fishmonger's".

items.prompt: The butcher's shop = ___ (full word, singular with article).
items.explanation: From *haragi* (meat) + *-tegi* (place, a variant of *-degi*) + *-a* (the article).

items.prompt: How do you ask for the price of a product?
items.explanation: "Zenbat balio du?" is literally "how much is it worth?". "Zenbat da?" is also used more colloquially.

items.prompt: "Kiloa zortzi eurotan dago" means…
items.explanation: "X eurotan dago" — "it is X euros" (current price in the store).

items.prompt: "How much is it?" (when paying) in Basque = ___ da?
items.explanation: *Zenbat da?* is the short and very common formula for "how much is it?" at the end of a purchase.

items.prompt: "The kilo is 5 euros" = Kiloa bost ___ dago.
items.explanation: For prices "at X euros", the plural inessive *eurotan* ("in euros") is used.

items.prompt: What do you say to ask for something politely in a shop?
items.explanation: "Jarriko al didazu… mesedez?" = "Can you give me..., please?". A polite and common structure.
options: Jarriko al didazu kilo bat sagar, mesedez?

items.prompt: "Hartuko dut" means…
items.explanation: *Hartuko dut* — future tense of *hartu* (to take). It's used to confirm the purchase.

items.prompt: To ask for your turn: "Who's last, please?" → ___, mesedez?
items.explanation: *Azkena, mesedez?* is the universal formula for asking who is last in a queue.

items.prompt: Shopkeeper: "Anything else?" in Basque = "___?"
items.explanation: *Besterik?* or *Besterik nahi duzu?* — "anything else?" / "do you want anything else?"

items.prompt: "A kilo of apples" in Basque is…
items.explanation: In Basque, the quantity goes **first** and the product is used without an article: *kilo bat sagar*.

items.prompt: "A dozen eggs" in Basque is…
items.explanation: "*Dozena bat*" follows the same pattern as *kilo bat*: quantity + product without an article.

items.prompt: "Half a kilo of tomato" = kilo ___ tomate.
items.explanation: *Kilo erdi* — "half a kilo". *Erdi* (half) goes AFTER the unit, the opposite of how it works in English.

items.prompt: "More" in Basque (to ask for a bit more at the shop) = ___.
items.explanation: *Gehiago* (more) and *gutxiago* (less) are the two basic comparatives for adjusting quantities.

items.prompt: You're at the fruit shop. How do you ask for half a kilo of apples?
items.explanation: Pattern: quantity + product without the article: **kilo erdi sagar** (half a kilo of apples).

items.prompt: "There is no bread" is said…
items.explanation: With negation + indefinite object, the partitive *-rik* is used: **ogi-rik**.

items.prompt: "How much is everything?" = Zenbat da ___?
items.explanation: *Dena* means "everything".

items.prompt: To ask if they have a product: "Do you have milk?" = Esne___ ba(d)aukazue?
items.explanation: Question of existence with an indefinite object = partitive **-rik** (esne**rik**).

items.prompt: How do you ask for a table for two?
items.explanation: "Mahai bat bi lagunentzat" = "a table for two people". *-entzat* indicates the plural recipient.

items.prompt: "Erreserba egin nahi dut" means…
items.explanation: *Erreserba egin* — "to make a reservation". *Nahi dut* — "I want".
options: I want to make a reservation

items.prompt: The waiter asks: "In whose name?" = "___ izenean?"
items.explanation: *Noren?* — interrogative genitive: "whose?". *Noren izenean?* is the standard formula.

items.prompt: "For tomorrow night" = Bihar ___
items.explanation: *Gau* (night) + *-rako* (for) → *gauerako* — "for the night".

items.prompt: "Lehen platera" means…
items.explanation: *Lehen platera* — first course. *Lehen* means "first".

items.prompt: "Postrea" in English is…
items.explanation: *Postrea* — dessert. The translation is straightforward.

items.prompt: "Menu of the day" = Eguneko ___
items.explanation: *Eguneko menua* — literally "the menu of the day" (eguneko = of the day).

items.prompt: You order "salad and fish". The waiter confirms: "Hasteko, entsalada eta bigarrenerako, ___."
items.explanation: *Arraina* — fish. *Bigarrenerako* — "for the second (course)".

items.prompt: "For starters, I'll have salad" is said…
items.explanation: *Hasteko* (to start) + *entsalada hartuko dut* (I'll have salad). Typical structure.

items.prompt: "For me, the fish" is said…
items.explanation: *Niretzat* — "for me" (recipient). It's the natural phrase to use when ordering at a shared table.

items.prompt: To ask "and for you?" to your companion = Eta ___?
items.explanation: *Zuretzat* — "for you" (the standard singular form).

items.prompt: "For the main course, meat" = Bigarrenerako, ___
items.explanation: *Bigarrenerako* — "for the main course (for the second course)". *Haragia* — the meat.

items.prompt: How do you ask for the bill?
items.explanation: *Kontua, mesedez* is the universal way to ask for the bill.

items.prompt: "Kobratuko al didazu?" means…
items.explanation: *Kobratu* — to charge; *al* — question particle; *didazu* — "(you) me/to me". Polite form.

items.prompt: "Can I pay by card?" = Txartelaz ___ dezaket?
items.explanation: *Ordaindu* — to pay. *Ordain dezaket?* — "can I pay?".

items.prompt: "I don't have change" = Ez ___ kanbiorik.
items.explanation: *Daukat* — "I have" (from *eduki*). With negation + indefinite object → *kanbio**rik***.

items.prompt: How do you propose to a friend "do you want to come for dinner?"
items.explanation: *Etorri nahi duzu...?* — "do you want to come...?". *Afaltzera* = "to dinner" (NORA case with a verb).

items.prompt: "Okay, what time shall we meet?" is said...
items.explanation: *Ados* — okay. *Geratuko gara* — "we will meet" (future tense of *geratu*).

items.prompt: "I can't, I have work tomorrow" = Ezin dut, bihar ___ dut.
items.explanation: *Lana dut / lan egin behar dut* — "I have work / I have to work".

items.prompt: "We'll meet at nine" = ___ geratuko gara.
items.explanation: *Bederatzietan* — "at nine" (inessive plural case for hours).

items.prompt: "Monday" in Basque is…
items.explanation: *Astelehena* — first day of the week (literally "first-day-of-the-week").

items.prompt: What day is "asteburua"?
items.explanation: *Asteburua* — weekend, literally "the end of the week".

items.prompt: "I go to the gym on Monday" = ___ kiroldegira noa.
items.explanation: *-(e)an* on days = "on". *Astelehenean* — "on Monday".

items.prompt: "Every Monday" = ___
items.explanation: The suffix *-ero* means "each / every": *astelehenero* = "every Monday".

items.prompt: "Tomorrow" in Basque is…
items.explanation: *Bihar* — tomorrow (the next day).

items.prompt: "The day after tomorrow" is…
items.explanation: *Etzi* — the day after tomorrow. It's a short and very useful word.

items.prompt: "Next week" = ___ astean.
items.explanation: *Datorren* — "the next" or "the coming one" (literally: "that comes"). *Datorren astean* is the standard form.

items.prompt: "When are you coming?" = ___ zatoz?
items.explanation: *Noiz?* — interrogative particle for "when?".

items.prompt: 'I will go to Bilbao tomorrow' is...
items.explanation: *Joango naiz* — future of *joan* (to go): particle *-go* + auxiliary *naiz*.

items.prompt: What is the future of "ikusi" (to see)?
items.explanation: Verbs ending in *-i* add *-ko*: *ikusi → ikusiko*.

items.prompt: "Tomorrow I will see it" = Bihar ikusi___ dut.
items.explanation: *Ikusi* + *-ko* = *ikusiko*. The particle *-ko* marks the future.

items.prompt: "I will go with you (pl.)" = Zuekin joan___ naiz.
items.explanation: *Joan* + *-go* (because it ends in -n) = *joango*. The particle *-go* is used after a nasal consonant.

items.prompt: "I'm meeting Mikel tomorrow" is…
items.explanation: *Mikel + -ekin* (with) = *Mikelekin*. *Geratuko naiz* — I will meet.

items.prompt: "I have a meeting at five" =…
items.explanation: In Basque, the word order is flexible: *Bostetan bilera dut* and *Bilera dut bostetan* are both correct.

items.prompt: "What time shall we meet?" = ___ ordutan geratuko gara?
items.explanation: *Zer ordutan?* — "what time?" (literally: "at what hour?").

items.prompt: "Around nine" = Bederatziak ___
items.explanation: *Aldera* — "around", "about". *Bederatziak aldera* — "around nine".

items.prompt: "Tomorrow I'll go to the gym" =…
items.explanation: Future tense: *joan + go = joango* + *naiz* (I). *Kiroldegira* = to the gym (-ra suffix for destination).

items.prompt: "On Saturday I'll meet Maialen for coffee" =…
items.explanation: *Larunbatean* (on Saturday) + *Maialenekin* (with Maialen) + *geratuko naiz* (I will meet) + *kafea hartzeko* (to have coffee).
options: Larunbatean Maialenekin geratuko naiz kafea hartzeko

items.prompt: "Next week I'll have exams" = ___ astean azterketak izango ditut.
items.explanation: *Datorren* — "next". *Datorren astean* — "next week".

items.prompt: "On Friday I'll go out with friends" = Ostiralean lagunekin atera___ naiz.
items.explanation: *Atera* + *ko* + *naiz* = *aterako naiz* (I will go out). Verb ending in -a → -ko.

items.prompt: We live in Pamplona = gu Iruñean bizi ___.
items.explanation: Bizi izan takes NOR: ni bizi naiz, gu bizi gara.

items.prompt: Do you have siblings? = senide___ baduzu?
items.explanation: Partitive -rik in questions: seniderik baduzu?, dirurik baduzu?

items.prompt: "I like apples" = …
items.explanation: Plural (sagarrak) → zaizkit. Never dut/naiz with gustatzen: the mistake the exam hunts with a magnifying glass.

items.prompt: I go home by bus = etxe___ noa autobusez.
items.explanation: Allative -ra (to/towards): etxera noa. The instrumental -z (autobusez) is already given.

items.prompt: I'm coming from the beach = hondartza___ nator.
items.explanation: Ablative -tik (from): hondartzatik nator. The partner of -ra: I go TO / I come FROM.

items.prompt: "I work with my brother" = …
items.explanation: Comitative -rekin (with): anaiarekin. *-rentzat* would be FOR him; *-ren*, his; *-ra*, towards him (!).

items.prompt: Which one is CORRECT?
items.explanation: Numeral + BARE noun: hiru liburu (three books), no article. And plural on the verb: ditut.

items.prompt: "It's half past three" = …
items.explanation: Hirurak eta erdiak dira. Hours go in plural: ordu batA is the exception (singular).

items.prompt: This book is Ane's (possession) = liburu hau Ane___ da.
items.explanation: Genitive -ren + article: Anerena (Ane's one). With a noun: Aneren liburua.

items.prompt: A well-formed question to answer "Okindegian erosten dut ogia":
items.explanation: Answer in -n (okindegiAN, place) → question NON (where). Nora = where to (movement).

items.prompt: I want coffee with milk = kafea esne___ nahi dut.
items.explanation: Comitative with a word ending in -e: esne + arekin = esnearekin.

items.prompt: We're going to the market = merkatu___ goaz.
items.explanation: Allative -ra with goaz: merkatura goaz.

items.prompt: "I don't have time" = …
items.explanation: Ez daukat denborarik: negation + partitive. Naiz/nago don't work for HAVING.

items.prompt: "Tomorrow I'll buy bread" (A1 future) = …
items.explanation: Bihar + erosiKO dut (the -ko future from unit 13). "Erosi dut" would mean already bought; "atzo" (yesterday) + future is impossible.

items.prompt: How much does the cheese cost? = zenbat ___ du gaztak?
items.explanation: Zenbat balio du? — the price question. The NORK (gaztaK) is already given in the sentence.

items.prompt: At the restaurant, to order politely:
items.explanation: "Ura, mesedez" — the thing you order + mesedez is the perfect A1 formula. The first is a blunt command; the third asks backwards.

items.prompt: I have to study = ikasi ___ dut.
items.explanation: Behar dut = I have to: ikasi behar dut, joan behar dut.

items.prompt: "Where is the bathroom?" = …
items.explanation: Non dago…? — location with egon. Survival question number 1.

items.prompt: Put the sentence in order: [gustatzen / kafea / zait / asko]
items.explanation: Kafea asko gustatzen zait — the neutral order: NOR + asko + gustatzen + NOR-NORI.

items.prompt: On Mondays I go to Basque class = astelehen___ euskara-klasera joaten naiz.
items.explanation: Days in the habitual plural: astelehenETAN (on Mondays), ostiraletan (on Fridays).

readings.title: Ane
readings.html:
Kaixo! Ni Ane naiz, lekeitiarra, baina orain Bilbon bizi naiz, alde zaharrean, pisu txiki batean. 28 urte ditut. Erizaina naiz eta ospitale batean egiten dut lan, gauez; horregatik goizetan lo egiten dut. Arratsaldeak niretzat dira: asteartetan eta ostegunetan pilotan jokatzen dut frontoian, asteazkenetan euskara-klasera joaten naiz, eta ostiraletan kuadrillarekin afaltzen dut Deustuko taberna batean.

Familia txikia daukat: aita, ama eta ahizpa bat, 31 urtekoa. Gurasoak Lekeition bizi dira, itsaso ondoan; aita arrantzalea da. Asteburuetan haiengana joaten naiz: amaren tortilla asko gustatzen zait — munduko onena da! Ahizpa Gasteizen bizi da, eta hilean behin elkartzen gara.

questions.prompt: According to the text, where is Ane from?
questions.explanation: "Lekeitiarra naiz" — I'm from Lekeitio. In Bilbao she LIVES (bizi naiz). Origin (nongoa) ≠ residence (non bizi): the A1's star distinction.

questions.prompt: When does Ane work?
questions.explanation: "Gauez egiten dut lan" — I work at night. That's why she sleeps in the mornings.

questions.prompt: What does Ane do on Fridays?
options: She has dinner with her friends
questions.explanation: "Ostiraletan kuadrillarekin afaltzen dut" — on Fridays I have dinner with my friend group. Pelota is Tuesdays and Thursdays.

questions.prompt: How old is her sister?
questions.explanation: "Ahizpa bat daukat, 31 urtekoa". Ane is 28; the sister, 31. The exam ALWAYS crosses data to catch you.

questions.prompt: What does Ane like a lot?
questions.explanation: "Amaren tortilla asko gustatzen zait — munduko onena da!" — her mother's tortilla, the best in the world.

readings.title: Iragarkia — kiroldegia
readings.html:
HERRIKO KIROLDEGIA — IZENA EMAN!

Ordutegia: astelehenetik ostiralera, 8:00-21:00. Larunbatetan 9:00-14:00. Igandeetan itxita.

Igerilekua: astelehenetik ostiralera, 8:00-21:00. Gimnasioa eta pilotalekua: ordutegi osoan.

Prezioak: 25 euro hilean. Ikasleak: 18 euro hilean. 65 urtetik gorakoak: doan!

Izena emateko: NANa eta argazki bat ekarri harrerara. Informazio gehiago: 948 123 456.

questions.prompt: Which day is the sports centre closed?
questions.explanation: "Igandeetan itxita" — closed on Sundays. *Itxita* (closed) ↔ *irekita* (open).

questions.prompt: How much do students pay per month?
questions.explanation: "Ikasleak: 18 euro hilean". The 25 € is the regular rate. Reading prices calmly wins exams.

questions.prompt: You want to swim on a Tuesday. At what time can you?
questions.explanation: Pool "astelehenetik ostiralera, 8:00-21:00" — Tuesday falls within "Monday to Friday"; 8:00 yes, 7 not yet and 22:30 no longer.

questions.prompt: What do you need to bring to sign up?
questions.explanation: "NANa eta argazki bat ekarri" — bring your ID and a photo. *Ekarri* = to bring.

questions.prompt: Who pays NOTHING?
questions.explanation: "65 urtetik gorakoak: doan!" — over-65s, free. *Doan* = free, a golden word on any poster.

readings.title: Jonen mezua
readings.html:
Kaixo, Miren!

Zer moduz? Larunbatean gure etxean bazkalduko dugu, familia osoa. Amak paella egingo du — bai, paella, gure amak! 😄 Etorri nahi duzu?

Ordu batean gure etxean, Alde Zaharrean. Ardoa eta ogia guk jarriko ditugu. Ekarri zuk postrea, mesedez!

Erantzun laster, mesedez. Ondo izan!

Jon

questions.prompt: Why does Jon write the message?
options: To invite her for lunch on Saturday
questions.explanation: "Larunbatean gure etxean bazkalduko dugu… etorri nahi duzu?" — a lunch invitation for Saturday.

questions.prompt: At what time are they meeting?
questions.explanation: "Ordu batean gure etxean" — at one. "Half past one" would be *ordu bat eta erdietan*.

questions.prompt: What does Jon's family provide?
options: The paella, the wine and the bread
questions.explanation: The mother makes the paella and "ardoa eta ogia guk jarriko ditugu". Miren is only asked for the dessert.

questions.prompt: What must Miren do "laster"?
questions.explanation: "Erantzun laster, mesedez" — reply soon. *Erantzun* = to reply; *laster* = soon.

readings.title: Mirenen eguna
readings.html:
Nire egunak oso antzekoak dira. Lanegunetan seiak eta erdietan jaikitzen naiz. Dutxatu, gosaldu — kafea esnearekin eta ogi txigortua — eta zortziak laurden gutxitan etxetik ateratzen naiz. Oinez joaten naiz lanera; euria egiten badu, autobusez. Bulego batean egiten dut lan, bederatzietatik bostetara.

Arratsaldean, astearteetan eta ostegunetan euskara-klasera joaten naiz. Zortzietan afaltzen dut, eta afaldu eta gero, telesail bat ikusten dut eta pixka bat irakurtzen dut. Hamaiketan ohera.

Asteburuak beste kontu bat dira! Larunbat goizetan amarekin merkatura joaten naiz, eta larunbat gauetan lagunekin ateratzen naiz. Igandeetan, mendira — eta gero, siesta ederra. Zortzi eta erdietan jaikitzen naiz larunbatetan… luxu hutsa!

questions.prompt: At what time does Miren get up on workdays?
questions.explanation: "Seiak eta erdietan jaikitzen naiz" — at half past six. The 8:30 is for weekends.

questions.prompt: How does Miren get to work?
options: On foot, and by bus if it rains
questions.explanation: "Oinez joaten naiz lanera; euria egiten badu, autobusez" — on foot; when it rains, by bus.

questions.prompt: What does Miren do after dinner?
questions.explanation: "Afaldu eta gero, telesail bat ikusten dut eta pixka bat irakurtzen dut" — a series and a bit of reading.

questions.prompt: On Saturday mornings Miren…
options: Goes to the market with her mother
questions.explanation: "Larunbat goizetan amarekin merkatura joaten naiz" — to the market with her mother.

readings.title: Iragarkia — herriko jaiak
readings.html:
HERRIKO JAIAK — EKAINAK 20-23

Ostirala 20: 19:00etan txupinazoa plazan; 22:00etan kontzertua (doan).

Larunbata 21: 12:00etan herri-bazkaria frontoian (10 euro; umeak, doan); 18:00etan pilota-partida.

Igandea 22: 11:00etan mendi-martxa; 20:00etan su artifizialak.

Astelehena 23: 17:00etan umeentzako jolasak; 21:00etan azken kontzertua.

Txartelak: herriko tabernan edo webgunean. Euria egiten badu, kontzertuak kiroldegian.

questions.prompt: How much does Friday's concert cost?
questions.explanation: "22:00etan kontzertua (doan)" — *doan* = free. If you like a Basque poster, it almost surely says *doan*.

questions.prompt: Where is Saturday's communal lunch?
questions.explanation: "Herri-bazkaria frontoian" — at the fronton (frontoiAN, the locative -n).

questions.prompt: If it rains, where are the concerts?
questions.explanation: "Euria egiten badu, kontzertuak kiroldegian" — if it rains, to the kiroldegi. *Badu* = if (basic conditional the A1 reads, not produces).

questions.prompt: What's on Sunday morning?
questions.explanation: "Igandea: 11:00etan mendi-martxa" — mountain walk. The fireworks (su artifizialak) are at night.

questions.prompt: Where are the tickets sold?
options: At the town tavern or on the website
questions.explanation: "Txartelak: herriko tabernan edo webgunean" — *edo* = or. *Txartela* = ticket/card.

readings.title: Postala — oporretatik
readings.html:
Kaixo, amona!

Zer moduz? Gu oso ondo! Donostian gaude, hondartza ondoko hotel txiki batean. Goizetan hondartzara joaten gara eta arratsaldetan alde zaharrean paseatzen dugu. Gaur goizean Aquariuma ikusi dugu — arrain pila bat!

Eguraldi ona egiten du: eguzkia egunero! Pintxoak jaten ditugu gauero — garestiak, baina zoragarriak. Ostiralean etxera itzuliko gara.

Muxu handi bat,

Maite eta Ander

questions.prompt: Where are Maite and Ander?
options: In Donostia, next to the beach
questions.explanation: "Donostian gaude, hondartza ondoko hotel txiki batean" — *ondoko* = next to.

questions.prompt: What do they do in the mornings?
questions.explanation: "Goizetan hondartzara joaten gara" — the old town is in the afternoon. They cross the times of day on purpose.

questions.prompt: What have they done today?
questions.explanation: "Gaur goizean Aquariuma ikusi dugu" — recent perfect (ikusi dugu): TODAY's thing.

questions.prompt: When do they go back home?
questions.explanation: "Ostiralean etxera itzuliko gara" — the -ko future: we WILL return on Friday.

listenings.title: Kafetegian
listenings.transcriptEu:
Miren: Egun on! Zer nahi duzu?
Jon: Kaixo! Kafe bat esnearekin, mesedez.
Miren: Zerbait jateko?
Jon: Bai, kruasan bat. Zenbat da?
Miren: Hiru euro eta berrogeita hamar.
Jon: Hartu, lau euro.
Miren: Eskerrik asko! Berrogeita hamar zentimo zuretzat.

questions.prompt: What does Jon order to drink?
questions.explanation: «Kafe bat esnearekin» — coffee with milk (esnea + -arekin).

questions.prompt: What does he order to eat?
questions.explanation: «Kruasan bat» — a croissant.

questions.prompt: How much does it all cost?
questions.explanation: «Hiru euro eta berrogeita hamar» — three euros fifty.

questions.prompt: How much does Jon pay with?
questions.explanation: «Hartu, lau euro» — here, four euros. The change: 50 cents.

listenings.title: Bi lagun kalean
listenings.transcriptEu:
Ane: Kaixo, Mikel! Zer moduz?
Mikel: Oso ondo, eta zu?
Ane: Ni ere ondo. Nora zoaz?
Mikel: Lanera noa. Bulego batean egiten dut lan, Bilbon.
Ane: Ni euskara-klasera noa, asteartero.
Mikel: Oso ondo! Gero arte, Ane!
Ane: Agur, Mikel!

questions.prompt: How is Mikel?
questions.explanation: «Oso ondo» — very well.

questions.prompt: Where is Mikel going?
questions.explanation: «Lanera noa» — I'm going to work.

questions.prompt: Where does Mikel work?
questions.explanation: «Bulego batean egiten dut lan, Bilbon» — at an office, in Bilbao.

questions.prompt: When does Ane go to Basque class?
questions.explanation: «Asteartero» — every Tuesday (astearte + -ro).

listenings.title: Tren-geltokian (megafonia)
listenings.transcriptEu: Arratsalde on. Donostiara doan trena laugarren bidetik aterako da, seiak eta erdietan. Trenak hamar minutuko atzerapena du. Txartelak leihatilan edo makinetan eros ditzakezue. Eskerrik asko.

questions.prompt: Where is the train going?
questions.explanation: «Donostiara doan trena» — the train going to Donostia.

questions.prompt: From which platform does it leave?
questions.explanation: «Laugarren bidetik» — from the fourth track (lau → laugarren).

questions.prompt: At what time does it leave?
questions.explanation: «Seiak eta erdietan» — at half past six.

questions.prompt: What's happening with the train?
questions.explanation: «Hamar minutuko atzerapena du» — it's running ten minutes late.

listenings.title: Supermerkatuan (megafonia)
listenings.transcriptEu: Arratsalde on, bezero maiteok. Gaur sagarrak eskaintzan daude: kiloa euro batean. Fruta-saila bigarren solairuan dago. Gogoratu: denda zortzietan itxiko dugu. Eskerrik asko eta ongi etorri!

questions.prompt: What's on offer today?
questions.explanation: «Sagarrak eskaintzan daude» — the apples are on offer.

questions.prompt: How much is a kilo?
questions.explanation: «Kiloa euro batean» — one euro per kilo.

questions.prompt: Where is the fruit section?
questions.explanation: «Bigarren solairuan» — on the second floor.

questions.prompt: At what time does the shop close?
questions.explanation: «Zortzietan itxiko dugu» — we'll close at eight.

listenings.title: Aitonaren mezua (erantzungailua)
listenings.transcriptEu: Kaixo, maitea! Aitona naiz. Bihar herrira etorriko naiz, eguerdian. Elkarrekin bazkalduko dugu, ados? Mesedez, erosi ogia eta gazta. Ondo izan, laster arte!

questions.prompt: Who leaves the message?
questions.explanation: «Aitona naiz» — I'm the grandfather.

questions.prompt: When is he coming?
questions.explanation: «Bihar… eguerdian» — tomorrow, at noon.

questions.prompt: What plan does he propose?
questions.explanation: «Elkarrekin bazkalduko dugu» — we'll have lunch together (bazkaldu = midday meal).

questions.prompt: What needs to be bought?
questions.explanation: «Erosi ogia eta gazta» — buy bread and cheese.

listenings.title: Lagunaren audio-mezua
listenings.transcriptEu: Aupa! Entzun: gaur ezin dugu zazpietan geratu. Nire anaia berandu aterako da lanetik. Zortzietan geratuko gara, ados? Eta plaza berrian, ez zaharrean — euria egingo du eta han aterpea dago. Erantzun, mesedez!

questions.prompt: At what time do they FINALLY meet?
questions.explanation: «Zortzietan geratuko gara» — the new time: eight. Seven is cancelled.

questions.prompt: Why does the plan change?
questions.explanation: «Nire anaia berandu aterako da lanetik» — his brother gets off work late.

questions.prompt: Where do they meet?
questions.explanation: «Plaza berrian, ez zaharrean» — in the new square, not the old one.

questions.prompt: What will the weather be like?
questions.explanation: «Euria egingo du» — it's going to rain (that's why they pick a covered spot/aterpe).

writings.title: Zure burua aurkeztu
writings.task: Introduce yourself in 6-8 sentences: who you are, where you're from and where you live, age, work/studies, two things from your week, something about your family and something you like. Write it BEFORE looking at the model.
writings.model: Kaixo! Mikel naiz, iruindarra, eta Txantrean bizi naiz, Iruñean. 35 urte ditut. Irakaslea naiz eta eskola batean egiten dut lan. Astelehenetan eta asteazkenetan igerilekura joaten naiz, eta larunbatetan mendira. Emaztea eta bi seme ditut. Gurasoak Lizarran bizi dira. Asteburuetan haiekin bazkaltzen dugu, eta amaren paella asko gustatzen zait!

checks.label: naiz to introduce yourself (Ane naiz, iruindarra naiz…)
dut / ditut (what you have or do)
At least two different cases: -rekin, -ra, locative -n

writings.title: Fitxa bete
writings.task:
The sports centre gives you a form. Fill it in in Basque with YOUR details:
Izen-abizenak · Adina · Herria · Telefonoa (in words, e.g. «bederatzi-lau-zortzi…») · Zein kirol gustatzen zaizu?
writings.model: Izen-abizenak: Ane Etxeberria · Adina: 28 urte · Herria: Lekeitio · Telefonoa: sei-bat-zazpi-bederatzi-zero-bi-lau-hiru-zortzi · Kirola: igeriketa gustatzen zait

checks.label: The phone number in words (six number-words or more)

writings.title: Erantzun gonbidapenari
writings.task: A friend invites you for lunch on Saturday at his place (at one, you bring the dessert). Answer in 4-6 sentences: greet, accept or decline with a reason, ask something and say goodbye. Write it before looking at the models.
writings.model:
Baietz: Kaixo, Jon! Bai, noski, joango naiz! Paella asko gustatzen zait. Postrea nik ekarriko dut: amaren tarta. Ardo beltza ala zuria edango dugu? Larunbatera arte!

Ezetz: Kaixo, Jon! Mila esker, baina larunbatean ezin dut: lan egiten dut. Hurrengoan bai, ados? Ondo pasa eta on egin!

checks.label: Greeting AND farewell (Kaixo… / agur, ondo izan, laster arte…)

writings.title: Zure eguna
writings.task: Describe YOUR work or study day in 6-8 sentences, with at least: an exact time, a means of transport, a meal and something from the afternoon.
writings.model: Lanegunetan zazpietan jaikitzen naiz. Kafea hartzen dut eta autobusez joaten naiz lanera. Bulego batean egiten dut lan, zortzietatik hiruretara. Eguerdian etxean bazkaltzen dut. Arratsaldean kirola egiten dut eta erosketak egiten ditut. Gauean familiarekin afaltzen dut eta telesail bat ikusten dut.

checks.label: A means of transport (oinez, autobusez, kotxez, bizikletaz…)

writings.title: Postal batetik
writings.task: You're on holiday. Write a 5-6 sentence postcard to a friend: where you are, what you do every day, one thing you HAVE DONE today, what the weather is like and when you're coming back.
writings.model: Kaixo, Maddi! Donostian nago, lagunekin. Goizetan hondartzara joaten gara eta arratsaldetan paseatzen dugu. Gaur Aquariuma ikusi dugu — zoragarria! Eguraldi ona egiten du, eguzkia egunero. Igandean etxera itzuliko naiz. Muxu bat!

checks.label: Where you are: …-n nago / gaude (Donostian nago)
Something from TODAY in the perfect (ikusi dut, jan dugu…)
When you return, in the future (itzuliko naiz…)

writings.title: Zure etxea
writings.task: Describe your home in 6 sentences: where you live, how many rooms it has (zenbat logela), your favourite room and why, what there is in the kitchen, and something there ISN'T.
writings.model: Iruñean bizi naiz, pisu batean. Etxeak hiru logela ditu eta bi komun. Nire logela handia da eta leiho handi bat dauka — asko gustatzen zait. Sukaldean mahai bat, lau aulki eta hozkailu zahar bat daude. Balkoirik ez daukagu, baina berdin da: etxe polita da!

checks.label: dago / daude for what there is
A number + thing (hiru logela, bi komun…)
Something there ISN'T (ez dago / ez daukat / -rik)
